YES

The plan casts exactly the 112 projection matrices (16 layers × 7 named matrices) to bfloat16, leaves every other tensor untouched at float32 (the leading `.* → float32` cast is a no-op on an all-float32 input and is value-preserving), deletes nothing, renames nothing, and writes `out/T3` as sharded safetensors with a 256 MiB shard budget so that each oversized embedding/lm_head tensor lands alone. All four required checks fail loudly before the write: the pre-cast `count … is: 114`-style count of the 112-matcher plus the post-cast dtype asserts (112 matched tensors bfloat16, everything else float32 via the anchored negative lookahead) together enforce "exactly 112 bfloat16", and the explicit `q_proj` bfloat16, `embed_tokens` float32, and total-count-114 asserts are present verbatim.
